title: Targeted Counterfactual Branch Augmentation for Robust Text-Based World Models under Agent Policy Shift

contributions.purpose: Improve text-based world model robustness under agent policy shift without expensive multi-agent trajectory collection.
contributions.mechanism: Targeted Counterfactual Branch Augmentation (TCBA) generates counterfactual branches weighted by the out-of-distribution agent's action distribution, using targeting weights computed from OOD agent calibration runs.
contributions.evaluation: On ScienceWorld, TCBA improves consistency ratio by 50.4% over random branching (0.385 vs 0.256) and 28.8% over expert-only training.
contributions.source_quote: We propose TCBA, a low-cost method for improving world model robustness under policy shift that requires only environment-instrumented counterfactual branches rather than multi-agent trajectory collection.

contributions.purpose: Show that targeting, not branching per se, drives the robustness gain.
contributions.mechanism: Comparison of random counterfactual branching versus TCBA's OOD-weighted targeted branching on ScienceWorld.
contributions.evaluation: Random branching does not improve world model robustness and may hurt performance, while TCBA achieves 50.4% consistency-ratio improvement over random branching.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that targeting is necessary: random counterfactual branching does not improve world model robustness and may actually hurt performance, while TCBA achieves 50.4% improvement in consistency ratio over random branching.

contributions.purpose: Verify the targeting mechanism actually matches the deployment agent's behavior distribution.
contributions.mechanism: Analysis comparing KL divergence between generated branch distributions and OOD agent action distributions for targeted versus random branching.
contributions.evaluation: TCBA's targeting achieves 58.2% lower KL divergence to the OOD action distribution compared to random branching.
contributions.source_quote: We provide analysis showing the targeting mechanism successfully aligns branch distribution with OOD agent behavior, achieving 58.2% lower KL divergence to the OOD action distribution.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work differs by introducing a targeting mechanism that biases counterfactual generation toward actions likely to be taken by OOD agents.

Our approach shares the intuition of branching from expert data but focuses on world model training rather than policy learning, and introduces explicit targeting toward OOD agent behavior rather than relying on random exploration.

Counterfactual data augmentation (Kim & Kim, 2022) offers a more efficient alternative by generating synthetic transitions from alternative actions, but random counterfactual sampling may not target the specific distribution shift that matters for deployment.

notes: Statistically inconclusive results, self-declared in the abstract: 'While results are promising, they are statistically inconclusive due to limited power (n=3 seeds, ~2% base success rate).' Treat headline gains (50.4%, 28.8%) as underpowered.
